summary: The note examines the rise of phishing scams alongside the shift to remote work and remote learning, citing a CISA report of a 70% increase in attacks. It explains phishing variants, warning signs, and prevention tips for teens and families, and describes how schools, companies and technology are responding. It concludes that phishing is an ongoing challenge requiring education, awareness and proactive security practices.
one_line: Phishing attacks have surged with remote work, targeting even teens studying from home, and defenses depend on education, MFA, institutional policy and technology.
key_facts: A CISA report published on September 15, 2023 cited a 70% increase in phishing attacks since many companies adopted remote work policies.
The large-scale move to remote work began in early 2020, and IT departments worldwide have faced a surge in cyber threats since then.
The upsurge is attributed largely to less secure networks used by remote workers and the psychological effect of being outside a traditional office environment.
Teens studying from home are increasingly targeted because cybercriminals see them as vulnerable entry points into household networks.
The FBI has noted cases where students unknowingly divulged a parent's work credentials or enabled malware installations that compromised entire systems.
Phishing is a technique in which a perpetrator masquerades as a trustworthy entity to obtain sensitive data such as passwords, credit card numbers and social security numbers.
Common phishing types include email phishing, spear phishing (personalized attacks), smishing (SMS), vishing (voice calls) and whaling (aimed at executives).
Warning signs include suspicious sender addresses or URLs, urgent or threatening language, unsolicited requests for information, and odd formatting or misspellings.
Recommended preventive measures for teens and families are keeping software up to date, using multi-factor authentication, regularly changing strong unique passwords, and education and training.
Schools should provide training, maintain secure networks and encourage school-provided secure platforms rather than insecure third-party applications.

Ellen Miles, CISO of TechForward Inc., whose comments were reported on October 3, 2023, stressed employee knowledge, regular cybersecurity training and clear channels for reporting suspicious activity.

Technologies against phishing include advanced email filtering, browsers with updated security features that warn about suspicious sites, and AI-powered measures that adapt to new phishing strategies.
